title: st.tabs: widget rerun inside a tab renders all tabs' content stacked below the page (regression in 1.59.0)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

**Regression in 1.59.0** (1.58.0 is fine): when a widget inside an `st.tabs` tab triggers a rerun, the tab bar disappears and the content of **all** tabs renders stacked vertically down the page, as if the tabs container no longer exists. A browser reload restores the tabs until the next widget interaction.

Possibly related to the tabs DOM rework in 1.59.0: in 1.58.0 each tab renders a `[data-baseweb="tab-panel"]` element (4 tabs → 4 panels, 1 visible); in 1.59.0 those elements are gone entirely.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import altair as alt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

st.title("Tabs regression repro")

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
df = pd.DataFrame({"x": range(20), "y": rng.rand(20)})


def tab_content(name: str) -> None:
    st.metric("Metric", name)
    st.dataframe(df.head(3))
    st.altair_chart(alt.Chart(df).mark_bar().encode(x="x:O", y="y:Q"), use_container_width=True)
    st.altair_chart(alt.Chart(df).mark_line().encode(x="x:O", y="y:Q"), use_container_width=True)
    st.subheader("Leaderboard")
    choice = st.selectbox("Date range", ["A", "B", "C"], key=f"{name}_sel")
    n = {"A": 5, "B": 10, "C": 15}[choice]
    st.altair_chart(alt.Chart(df.head(n)).mark_bar().encode(x="y:Q", y="x:O"), use_container_width=True)


names = ["All", "Indy", "Clarksville", "Fort Wayne"]
for tab, name in zip(st.tabs(names), names):
    with tab:
        tab_content(name)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. `pip install streamlit==1.59.0 altair` and run the app above.
2. Stay on the first tab ("All").
3. Change the "Date range" selectbox from "A" to "B".

### Expected Behavior

The rerun re-renders the first tab's content in place; the other three tabs stay hidden behind the tab bar (this is the 1.58.0 behavior).

### Current Behavior

After the rerun the tab bar vanishes and the content of all four tabs is appended down the page in sequence. Measured headlessly (Playwright, counting `[data-testid="stVegaLiteChart"]` elements with a non-null `offsetParent`): 3 charts visible before the selectbox change, all 12 visible after. The same script against 1.58.0 shows 3 before / 3 after.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version (1.58.0).

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.59.0 (broken), 1.58.0 (works)
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: reproduced on both macOS 15 and Raspberry Pi OS (Linux/arm64)
- Browser: Chrome, and headless Chromium via Playwright

comments.body:
### Triage summary

This is a **frontend regression in `st.tabs`** introduced in 1.59.0: when a widget inside a tab triggers a rerun, the tab bar disappears and the content of *all* tabs renders stacked vertically down the page.

**Likely root cause:** PR #15328 ("Remove `BaseWeb` for `Tabs`") reworked the tabs DOM, replacing the old BaseWeb implementation (`[data-baseweb="tab-panel"]`) with `react-aria-components`. This change first shipped in the `1.58.1.dev20260529` builds and was released as **1.59.0**, which matches the reporter's "works in 1.58.0, broken in 1.59.0" observation and the note that the `[data-baseweb="tab-panel"]` elements are gone.

In the new implementation (`frontend/lib/src/components/elements/Tabs/`), inactive tab panels are force-mounted (`shouldForceMount`) and hidden **solely** via the CSS rule `&[inert] { display: none }`, relying on `react-aria-components` to keep the `inert` attribute on every non-selected panel. The symptom (all panels visible only after a widget-triggered rerun, restored by a full page reload) is consistent with the non-selected panels losing their `inert` attribute when the tab's content re-renders, so `display: none` no longer applies and every panel's content stacks down the page. This should be reproducible/coverable in a unit or e2e test by asserting that non-active panels still carry `inert` (are hidden) after a widget interaction, not just on first mount.

### Related Issues

- **#11344** — [Custom components rendered in non-active tabs rendered with height of 0](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11344): Same area (rendering/visibility of non-active `st.tabs` panels). Not a duplicate, but the closest existing `st.tabs` rendering bug.
- **#15001** — [`st.vega_lite_chart` - width="stretch", behaves differently versions x>1.52.2](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15001): Another `type:regression` bug involving charts inside `st.tabs`; the repro here also uses Vega/Altair charts inside tabs, so worth cross-checking though the root cause differs.
- **#14492** — [Layout containers (tabs, expander, popover) should persist frontend state automatically without requiring key=](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14492): Related to how `st.tabs` frontend state is handled across reruns; tangential (an enhancement) but touches the same rerun/state area.

No exact duplicate of this specific 1.59.0 stacking regression was found among the open issues.
